reason: E1 supports that grain boundaries promote defect annihilation and that HEAs can enhance thermal stability, but it does not address laser remelting or post-annealing. E3 shows that nanocrystalline refractory HEAs can be fabricated with improved strength and stability, but uses co-sputtering, not laser remelting. E2 discusses defect recombination in HEAs but concerns a different alloy (HfTa) and irradiation-induced hardening, not surface nanostructuring. No cited evidence supports the specific intervention of laser remelting with post-annealing to create a stable nanocrystalline surface layer.
premises: Grain boundaries promote defect annihilation and reduce irradiation-induced defects
Nanocrystalline grains in pure materials suffer from thermal instability (coarsening)
HEAs can stabilize nanocrystalline structures against thermal coarsening
Laser remelting can create a nanocrystalline surface layer on refractory HEAs
Post-remelting annealing relieves residual stresses and stabilizes the nanocrystalline layer
